 EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL                        §
 SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION                 §                  Hearings.
 LINE PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET,                  §
 CONCHO, CORYELL, LAMPASAS,                     §
 LLANO, MASON, MCCULLOCH,                       §
 MENARD, MILAM, MILLS, SAN SABA,                §
 SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN, AND
 WILLIAMSON COUNTIES


Christine Thies, appearing pro se, submits this brief on behalf of herself (Intervenor 505)
and as representative for Thomas Thies and Brandon Whatley in this proceeding.

                                   I. INTRODUCTION

Although Alternative Link B22 is not among the Applicants currently identified ‘routes of
interest’ (894, 487, 296,392, 410, 572, 891), the issues raised in this proceeding extend
beyond any single route. The evidence presented demonstrates significant concerns
regarding notice, due process, property rights, and the Applicants' failure to establish
the necessity of this Project. As Texans, we understand that landownership and private
property rights are among our most fundamental values. The final decision in this
docket will have long-lasting consequences for affected landowners and communities
throughout the study area.

                               II. NOTICE DEFICIENCIES

The Applicants were required to provide notice to all landowners located within 500 feet
of a proposed alternative route by the statutory notice deadline. That deadline was
March 26, 2026. Despite owning property directly affected by the routing study area,

                                                                       Brief / Christine Thies
                                                                      PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                               SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                  Page 1 of 5
 neither I nor several neighboring property owners received notice until June 3, 2026 -
more than two months after the required notice date. The notice packet itself was
mailed by Oncor on June 1, 2026.




The Applicants contend that the failure to provide timely notice resulted from
inconsistencies in county appraisal district records. As reflected in Interchange Item No.
5595, Applicants acknowledged that the omission of our properties was identified
through intervenor testimony rather than through their own quality control procedures.

This explanation is not supported by the available geographic information system
("GIS") data. Both the LCRA and Oncor public-facing mapping applications failed to
accurately depict our subdivision. While a 2024 appraisal district data extract may have
predated the final platting of the subdivision, the 2025 Bell County Appraisal District
data correctly reflected the subdivision and associated parcels.

Applicants testified that they performed an initial data download in 2024 and an updated
download in 2025. Based upon my professional experience in GIS and spatial data


                                                                       Brief / Christine Thies
                                                                      PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                               SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                  Page 2 of 5
 management, the most plausible explanation is that Applicants updated ownership and
mailing-address records but failed to update the associated parcel geography. Such a
practice would be inconsistent with accepted GIS data management standards,
particularly given the availability of statewide parcel datasets maintained through Texas
Geographic Information Office. (https://data.geographic.texas.gov/)




The result was that affected landowners were deprived of timely notice and meaningful
participation during critical stages of route development. This deficiency is especially
significant because public participation and local input are essential components of the
evaluation of community values, landowner impacts, and routing alternatives.



                          III. FAILURE TO ESTABLISH NEED

Applicants have not satisfied their burden of proving the necessity of the proposed
transmission line.

The record demonstrates that fundamental questions regarding the underlying need for
this Project remain unresolved. In particular, the Motion to Defer Determination of Need

                                                                       Brief / Christine Thies
                                                                      PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                               SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                  Page 3 of 5
 filed by American Stewards of Liberty ("ASL") identifies several material issues that
continue to be actively contested, including:

          •   Whether ERCOT adequately evaluated reasonable alternatives to the
              Permian Basin Reliability Plan;
          •   Whether additional generation resources located closer to load centers could
              reduce or eliminate the need for portions of the proposed transmission
              expansion;
          •   Whether ERCOT's planning assumptions improperly relied upon the
              continued geographic separation of generation and load;
          •   Whether local generation alternatives received meaningful consideration; and
          •   Whether transmission expansion was effectively predetermined through
              modeling assumptions embedded within the Permian Basin Reliability Plan.

These concerns have not been raised solely by intervenors. The Commission itself has
questioned aspects of the need determination process and the assumptions underlying
the Permian Basin Reliability Plan. The existence of these unresolved questions weighs
against a finding that Applicants have met their burden under PURA to demonstrate that
this Project is necessary for the service, accommodation, convenience, or safety of the
public.

Where substantial uncertainty exists regarding the underlying need for a project of this
magnitude and cost, more thought and exploration should be conducted before
approving facilities that will impose permanent impacts upon Texas landowners and
communities.

                                      IV. CONCLUSION

For the foregoing reasons, the Administrative Law Judges should carefully consider the
deficiencies in notice, the resulting prejudice to affected landowners, and the unresolved
questions regarding project need. Applicants have not met their burden of




                                                                        Brief / Christine Thies
                                                                       PUC Docket No. 59475
                                                                SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349
                                                                                   Page 4 of 5
 demonstrating that the proposed Project satisfies the requirements of PURA and the
Commission's rules.
